Commentary.Commentary: Kane Williamson is handed the trophy and now the other players join him as they pose for the cameras. Right then! Done and dusted with the T20Is and New Zealand take the series home. It's time for the 3-match ODI series! The first match will be played on 17th August at 11.30 pm IST (6 pm GMT). Do join us early for the build up as well. Cheers!

Glenn Phillips is the PLAYER OF THE SERIES for his 134 runs at an average of 44 and a strike rate of 171. He says it feels good to come to Sabina Park and play well in front of an amazing crowd and amazing people. Says that they don’t know what the situation is and he backs his skill set and if the ball is to be put away he makes the most of it. Claims that they have a strong batting line up and with Neesham coming in towards the end he knows he can play freely. Goes on to mention that the bowlers have been the icing on the cake and have been doing well recently. Believes that they will come back strongly.

Brandon King is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH (53 runs off 35 balls). He says it is very special to do this at home in front of the supporters and his family was also present.  Mentions that consistency is the key and he wants to give the team a good start. Credits the bowlers by saying that they did an excellent job and made their job easier. Claims that his plan is the same no matter the total and that is to get a good start and set a platform. Adds that Brooks played excellently and understood the game. He didn’t take any risk and they batted well together. Admits that it is good to win leading to the World Cup and feels that they played well all around.

Kane Williamson, the captain of New Zealand starts by congratulating the Windies for the win. Says West Indies executed the plans well and outplayed them. Adds there is excitement while playing with this group. Mentions it's good to see the team progress and the focus has been always there. Shares that the World Cup is on the back of their mind but they keep thinking of the series and now they look forward to the ODI series.

Rovman Powell, the skipper of West Indies, says it is a dream to play for West Indies and captain in front of the crowd. Adds last night he asked the players for the support and they gave him. Shares that they talked about changing the bowlers and not loading them with 2-3 overs on a trot. It helps to keep them fresh. Thanks the crowd for their support. Applauds the effort of King, he says he played well and Brooks complimented him very well.
Presentation coming up...

New Zealand had something to bowl at but the bowlers were not up to the mark, the spinners especially. Kane Williamson will feel they could have taken the game deeper if the bowlers kept it tight. They were either too short or too full and were taken to the cleaners. Not the best of performance from the Kiwis but this shows there is still room for improvement. Earlier, New Zealand posted a par total. Only Glenn Phillips made a significant effort with the bat while the others struggled. Credit to the Windies bowlers who were tight and chipped in with wickets at regular intervals. It turned out to be an easy chase as the Kiwis found it hard to get the opening wicket and that took the game away.

A thumping win for West Indies! They have done well to avoid the whitewash. West Indies will have something to cherish and now will head into the ODI series with a positive mindset. It felt like West Indies could find it hard to bat on this sluggish pitch but the openers were absolutely brilliant getting a century partnership. Brandon King was the aggressor while Shamarh Brooks played the second fiddle. Both hit the loose balls and kept the required run rate in check. King fell after his fifty but by then they required a run-a-ball. Rovman Powell and Shamarh Brooks, in the end, chased down the target with ease.
SIX! The stand-in skipper hits the winning runs! Short of a length and on middle. Powell hangs back and pulls it over deep square leg for a biggie. West Indies win by 8 wickets.
Short in length and on middle. Powell looks to pull but misses.
On a good length and outside off, Rovman Powell cuts this to the right of backward point fielder who gets a hand to it and they get a couple of runs.
Full once again and in line with the stumps, Rovman Powell clips this to deep mid-wicket for a single.
A fraction full and outside off, Shamarh Brooks strokes this towards deep cover for a single.
James Neesham begins with a short ball wide outside off, Shamarh Brooks slashes this wide of deep cover and takes a couple of runs.
James Neesham to bowl now.
Short and wide outside off, Shamarh Brooks stands tall and pulls this towards deep mid-wicket.
Full delivery served on middle and leg, Rovman Powell clips this towards mid-wicket for a single.
SIX! What a hit! Tim Southee bowls this full and in line with the stumps, Rovman Powell shows immense power to just flick this over deep mid-wicket for a massive hit. Just 9 runs needed now.
Serves this one full and outside off, Shamarh Brooks knocks this to long off for a run.
Tim Southee serves this on a good length and angling into the pads, Shamarh Brooks looks to heave this leg side and misses. hits him high on his pad.
Tim Southee bowls this on a good length but angling down leg, Shamarh Brooks comes across to clip this but just misses the leg stump.
Bowls this full as well and just outside off, Shamarh Brooks works this to long on for a run.
Ish Sodhi flights this on full outside off, Rovman Powell sweeps this towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Rovman Powell plays a nice inside-out shot! Ish Sodhi flights this one full and outside off, Rovman Powell has room to lift this towards wide long on for four runs.

Continues bowling short and wide outside off, Shamarh Brooks cuts this to deep point for a single. Shamarh Brooks gets to his half-century. The slowest for West Indies in T20I but an important one nonetheless.
Short once again and outside off, Shamarh Brooks looks to cut this but misses.
Short and wide outside off, Rovman Powell pulls this towards long on for a single
On a good length and outside off, Rovman Powell works this towards third man to take a single and keep the strike.
Lockie Ferguson goes full and outside the off pole. Rovman Powell fends this towards point.
Back-of-a-length delivery outside the off stump, Shamarh Brooks gets on his toes and knocks it towards deep cover for a run.
This is on a good length and outside off, Rovman Powell guides this towards third man and takes a single.
FOUR! This has been thumped away! Lockie Ferguson goes full and outside off, Rovman Powell finds the gap between cover and mid off and the ball runs away to the deep cover fence for four runs.
Lockie Ferguson serves this on a good length and angling down leg, Shamarh Brooks looks to clip this and misses. The ball rolls to short fine leg and they take a leg bye.
Lockie Ferguson is back into the attack.
This is very full and outside off. Powell prods and drives it to covers. 32 needed in 30 runs.
This one lands outside off and turns away sharply. Powell leans and looks to defend but gets beaten on the outside edge.
On middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
The skipper Rovman Powell makes his way out to the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT! Thomas goes and New Zealand have two wickets in two overs! Sodhi floats one full and outside off. Thomas tries to slog-sweep but gets a top edge to deep mid-wicket where Glenn Phillips takes it. He tries to clear the longer side of the ground and also hit against the wind.
Commentary.Howout: c Glenn Phillips b Ish Sodhi

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and around off. Thomas dabs it to point.
FOUR! Drops it too short and on middle. Thomas pulls it in the air bt in the gap towards mid-wicket for a boundary.
Ish Sodhi has been given the ball once more. He has conceded 23 runs in his 2 overs.
Around off. Thomas punches off the back foot through covers for a single.
On middle. Blocked back to the bowler.
On the pads, it is flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Wide! A length ball, down the leg side. Brooks makes room to flick but misses. A wide is given.
On a length and around off. Brooks turns it to mid on.
FOUR! Stylish! Short of a length and outside off. Brooks swivels and pulls it to deep square leg for four.
Devon Thomas walks out to the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT! The magnificent partnership is finally broken! This is short and outside off. King looks to pull but gets a top edge to deep square leg. Martin Guptill there takes the skier. Brandon King goes after a superb knock. A bit too late with the wicket but another one can help New Zealand put some pressure.
Commentary.Howout: c Martin Guptill b Tim Southee

Commentary.Commentary: Tim Southee comes back into the attack. He has conceded 21 runs in his 2 overs.
Tossed up on off, pushed to covers.
Floated ball on middle, King forces it to deep mid-wicket for a single.

Three runs! A loopy ball, outside off, width is given there. Brooks chips it over the point fielder. The man from covers in deep runs across and dives to make a solid stop. He did really well to save a single. 100 up!
Tossed up on middle. King flicks it through square leg for a single.
On middle, it is worked to deep square leg for a single.
Flatter and outside off, it turns away and bounces. Brooks looks to cut but misses.
Mitchell Santner comes in to bowl his last over.
Angles it on the hips, it is bunted behind square leg for a single.
Shorter and around off, pulled to long on for a single.
Short of a length and outside off. King slashes and misses.
Uppish but safe! Full ball, outside off. Brooks drives it on the up and to the left of covers for one.
Length ball, outside off. Kept out.
A full ball on off. King pushes it to mid off and takes a quick single. With that single, King brings up his fifty. His 5th in T20I. What a knock in front of his home crowd.
Goes full this time and well outside off, Brandon King strokes this towards deep cover and takes another single.
A fraction short and outside off, Shamarh Brooks goes on the back foot and works the ball to deep mid-wicket for a run.
Michael Bracewell bowls this full and outside off, Shamarh Brooks goes for a reverse sweep and gets an inside edge through the keeper's legs for a couple of runs.
Michael Bracewell bowls this full as well and in line with the stumps, Brandon King works this towards deep mid-wicket and takes a single.
Michael Bracewell bowls this full and outside off, Shamarh Brooks drills this to the right of the bowler and a good stop at long on keeps them to a single.
Michael Bracewell bowls this full and angling into the pads, Brandon King works this towards short fine leg for a single.

Drinks break! A solid opening stand for West Indies have made them the favorites to win the game. Still, 61 runs needed in 60 balls and New Zealand will be aware of the fragile batting of the Windies. They need a couple of wickets to put pressure on them. Also, Michael Bracewell is back on.
A yorker now, outside off. Brooks fails to drive it away. 61 runs needed in 60 balls.
That was quick! A bouncer at 142 clicks on middle. Brooks ducks under it.
Touch fuller and outside off. Brooks chops it to backward point.
On a length and on middle and leg. Brooks tucks it to deep mid-wicket for a couple. A fumble allows them to take it with ease.
Outside off, dabbed to third man for one more.
On a length and outside off, Brooks punches it to covers for a single.
Lockie Ferguson is back on.

SIX! Make that three sixes in the over! This time from the blade of Brandon King. Ish Sodhi flights this one full outside off, Brandon King hits this well and gets the ball flying over the long on fence for a big hit. 19 runs from the over and this now looks easy for West Indies. They need 65 runs more to win.
Much better from Ish Sodhi as he bowls this a fraction short and outside off, Brandon King looks to slash at this and misses.
Ish Sodhi goes short once again and outside off, Shamarh Brooks pulls this to deep mid-wicket for a single.

SIX! Two in a row! Ish Sodhi compensates by going full and serves this outside off, Shamarh Brooks swings and lifts this over long on for another maximum. Shamarh Brooks is picking up his strike rate here.

SIX! BOOM! Shamarh Brooks wants to join the party! Ish Sodhi Bowls this short and in line with the stumps, Shamarh Brooks goes back in the crease and pulls this over the deep backward square leg fence for a huge hit.
Ish Sodhi serves this full and outside off, Shamarh Brooks gets a leading edge towards cover.
Loopy delivery served full and outside off, Shamarh Brooks knocks this to long on for a run.
Flights this one full and outside off, Shamarh Brooks gets a thick outside edge towards short third man.
An arm ball, slower and full on middle. King works it to mid-wicket for a single.
A loopy ball, outside off. Brooks punches it through covers for a single.
Shorter and outside off. King plays it late and delicately past short third man for a single.
SIX! Freebie for King and he makes the most of it! This is short and slanting on middle. King opens his body and pulls it over mid-wicket for a biggie.
Flights this full outside off, Shamarh Brooks knocks this back to the bowler.
Bowls this short and serves a googly. Shamarh Brooks pulls this one to deep mid-wicket as well and takes a run.
Serves this one short and outside the off stump, Shamarh Brooks mistimes his pull to long on for a single.
Short once gain and outside off, Brandon King pulls this towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
Ish Sodhi bowls this short and wide outside off, Shamarh Brooks slaps this to deep cover for a single.
Ish Sodhi starts with a googly angling into the pads, Shamarh Brooks looks to clip this leg side and misses. Hits his pad down leg side.
Full once again and angling into the stumps, Shamarh Brooks clips thisi to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Goes a fraction full and in line with the stumps, Brandon King clips this towards deep sqaure leg for a single.
Bowls this on a good length as well and outside off, Brandon King looks to cut and misses as the ball is too close.

FOUR! 14 runs from the first three balls! Tim Southee bowls this on a good length but wide outside off, Brandon King slashes at this and gets it through the gap as the ball flies towards the deep backward point fence for four more runs!
FOUR! This has been slapped away! Brandon King adjusts his length and goes short outside off, Brandon King pulls this towards deep square leg and collects four more runs.

SIX! BANG! Brandon King has got a hold of this one! Tim Southee serves this full and in line with the stumps, Brandon King clears the front leg out of the way and thumps this over deep mid-wicket for a biggie. Brandon King wants to get going here.
Tim Southee is back on. Went for 5 runs in his first over.
Another single as King fends this full ball to mid-wicket. 114 needed in 90 balls.
Around off, worked through covers for a single.

Santner serves an arm ball, short and makes it to straighten up on middle. Brooks was trying to pull but misses and gets hit right on the box. An appeal for LBW but the finger stays down. New Zealand take the review. UltraEdge shows no bat. The Ball Tracking shows the ball lobs over the middle pole. Not out.
Slower and on middle, it is flicked through square leg for a single.
FOUR MORE! Tossed up, outside off. King comes down the track and smashes it over the bowler's head for another four.
FOUR! King breaks the shackles! Flatter ball, angling on middle. King makes room and slaps it through covers, finds the gap for four.
Mitchell Santner has been brought into the attack. He conceded just three runs in his first over.
On a length and on middle. Brooks keeps it out. Excellent start by Lockie, just one runs off it.
Ferguson goes short now, outside off. Brooks leaps but fails to get his bat on it.
On a length and around middle, nips in. Brooks gets on his toes as he tries to play on the leg side but gets hit on the pads. An appeal but that was going down.
Short of a length and around off. Brooks gets inside the line of the ball and nudges but finds short fine leg.
On a length and around off. King knocks it to mid off and scampers across for a quick single.
On a length and on middle, extra bounce. King looks to flick it away but misses and gets hit high on the pads.
Lockie Ferguson has been given the ball now. New Zealand trying different bowlers every over.
On a length and around leg. Brooks steps across as he tries to tuck it away but misses.
On a length and outside off, slapped to sweeper cover for a single.
On the hips, nudged to square leg for a single.

FOUR LEG BYES! A huge appeal for LBW but clearly angling down! This is on a length and angling down the leg side. Brooks looks to flick but misses and it brushes his pads before rolling away from the keeper and to the fine leg fence.
FOUR! Finds the gap! On a length and outside off. Brooks opens the face of the bat in the last moment and dabs it away past backward point for a boundary. Right through the gap!
Starts with a fuller ball, around off. Brooks drives it to mid off.
Tim Southee has been brought into the attack now.
An arm ball, full and on off. King punches it to covers.
Full and on off, kept out.
On a length and outside off, pushed to covers.
Tossed up, outside off, spinning away. King tries to slog-sweep but miscues it to covers. He tried to play against the spins there.
Two wides! Tries to serve it quicker but does so down the leg side. Brooks fails to get his bat on it. The keeper fails to collect and the batters take a single.
Slides a full ball, quicker and on the pads. Brooks misses his flick and gets hit on the pads.
Fraction short and outside off. King works it to long off for one.
Spinner from the other end as well. Mitchell Santner will share the new ball.
Tossed up on middle, swept to short fine leg where Sodhi dives and gets a hand to it. It still rolls behind for a couple of runs.
Flatter ball, outside off. Brooks dabs it to backward point where Neesham makes a good stop.
FOUR! First boundary of the chase! This is too short and on middle. Brooks rocks back and pulls it past short fine leg for a boundary.
Slightly shorter and outside off. Brooks punches off the back foot but straight to covers.
Flatter and around off. Brooks gets behind the line and blocks it.
Shorter and on middle. King pulls it to deep square leg to get off the mark with a single.
